set.tovw: Lead grade C: counterfeiters' island named in two county histories and attested as 'Bogus Island' in 1880-81 local papers; no cache claimed, relic site
set.pl: Bogus Island, Fox River about 2 mi upstream (NE) of Algonquin toward Cary (1880 Sentinel); exact island not fixed
pinev: 1885 county history: 'about a mile further up the stream'; 1880 Sentinel: 'two miles above the village'. Pin follows the period paper, on the river reach between Algonquin and Cary. Not the Indiana Bogus Island (Beaver Lake, Newton Co), which most 'Bogus Island' hits refer to.
Measured 2 mi upstream along the Fox from the Algonquin crossing on the USA Rivers and Streams line (a generalized line, so within about 200 m of the channel); r1200.
set.st: The 1885 McHenry county history says counterfeiters frequenting Algonquin village 'were finally tracked to Bogus Island, about a mile further up the stream, where they were captured'; it was Allan Pinkerton's first detective case. The 1878 Kane County history tells Pinkerton's capture of 'Old Craig' (taken to Geneva), likely the same affair. Pin is about two miles up the Fox River from Algonquin, not the island itself. Local papers of 1880-81 place Bogus Island in the Fox two miles above Algonquin village, drowned to a rush bed while the dam pool stood and an island again when the dam breached; the name was in everyday use.
